answer: A random peer re-executes the job, and the reward converts into a slow vesting stream only when a quorum from unrelated subnetworks agrees, so a farm that owns one subnetwork still cannot release its own payout. Price it: every alias needs a distinct re-execution and a quorum seat outside its cluster, which puts the marginal cost of a fake identity above the present value of one epoch's nectar, while the quartz of a verified output and the walnut of its vesting schedule sit locked until the quorum signs.
